title: Answer Connectivity Queries on a Network
statement: You are given n nodes labeled 0 to n-1, a list of undirected edges where each edge is [u, v] meaning u and v are directly linked, and a list of queries where each query is [a, b]. First apply every edge, then answer every query. For each query [a, b], the answer is True if and only if a and b belong to the same connected component once all edges have been applied, and False otherwise. A node is always connected to itself, so a query [a, a] is always True. Return a list of booleans with exactly one entry per query, in the same order the queries are given. Edges may be repeated or listed in either direction; treat them all as undirected links.
hints: Every query asks the same thing repeatedly: do these two nodes end up in the same group after all the links are made? What structure lets you merge groups and test membership in near-constant time?

Use a disjoint-set (union-find) with a parent array. The invariant that matters: two nodes are in the same component exactly when they share the same ROOT, which you reach by following parent pointers to the top, not just looking one level up.

Initialize parent[i] = i. For each edge [u, v], union them by linking the root of one to the root of the other. To answer [a, b], compute find(a) and find(b) (walking to each root, ideally with path compression) and return find(a) == find(b). Build one boolean per query in input order.
